predicate.verdict_note: Third round. The only change is that scripts/check_release_t1_lanes_joined.sh reports by default and blocks under RELEASE_T1_LANES_ENFORCE=1. Verified: report mode exits 0 with a REPORT line on a mutated autopilot and on a moved mutant anchor; ENFORCE=1 exits 1 on both; ENV stays rc 2 in both modes; on the real tree it passes 8 cases and 11 of 11 mutants in report mode. The pattern matches check_release_draft_gated.sh except that a failing baseline exits at once and hides every mutant result in report mode, where the draft guard runs them all (measured; advisory). Nothing sets the ENFORCE variable, so the guard blocks nowhere, as with the draft guard; this is the L31 design but the gate is weaker than before by that switch. The choom and exit-75 reason gaps from the previous round remain. No new defect in the change.

findings.failure_scenario: When the baseline check (`check "$AUTOPILOT" real`) fails, the script calls `finish 1`, which exits the script immediately (with `0` in report mode and `1` in enforce mode). Because it exits early, it skips running all the mutant checks, completely hiding any mutant failures from the logs. In contrast, the reference script (`check_release_draft_gated.sh`) sets `bad=1` and continues running mutants.
findings.summary: Early exit on baseline failure hides mutant checks

findings.failure_scenario: When the script completes successfully (`fails=0`), it drops past the `[ "$fails" -eq 0 ] || finish 1` check and falls off the end of the script, implicitly exiting 0. It skips calling `finish 0`, unlike the reference script which explicitly calls `finish "$bad"`.
findings.summary: Success path skips the finish function
